card.hook: Most people join the queue without looking up, but the best bit of the front is above the door. Two painted figures, Art and Science, sit over the entrance arch, and the shop's name is lettered in bright colours right beneath them.

card.best_time: Early in the day or later in the afternoon is usually calmer, so you get fewer people in your shot. The front faces south, so around midday it's likely to be in strong sun.

card.good_to_know: Livraria Lello opened in 1906 and is one of the oldest bookshops in Portugal, often ranked among the best in the world. The facade mixes Neo-Gothic and Art Nouveau touches. card.hook: Porto Cathedral looks less like a church and more like a fortress that's had a good day: two square towers with little domes on top, and a plain, heavy front in between. It's the classic postcard shot, and it's easier to get than you'd think.
card.stand_here: Stand in the right-hand corner of Terreiro da Sé, the square in front of the cathedral, and face the cathedral front. From the square, the cathedral is to the north-east, about 1 minute on foot.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to fit both towers and the stone cross into one picture. Then try zoom 1x for a more natural look, and zoom 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) to home in on the rose window and the tower tops.
card.make_it_pop: Switch on the gridlines and keep your phone upright and level, so the towers stand up straight instead of leaning.
card.best_time: Go early in the morning, before the square fills up with other visitors. Take a few frames anyway in case someone wanders through.
card.selfie_here: Head to the big paved courtyard at the back of the cathedral, away from the main street, and face the river and Gaia. Use the front camera, try zoom 0.5x, and keep the cathedral over your shoulder with the open city view filling the frame. The Terreiro da Sé square also works, with the cathedral right beside you.
card.ask_someone: Stand in the middle of the square with the cathedral behind you, and ask your helper to shoot from the right-hand corner, facing the cathedral.
card.rules_and_safety: The cathedral is a place of worship, so check the official site before you go for visiting arrangements inside.
card.challenge: Get the stone cross low in the frame, the towers filling the top, and not one stranger walking through your shot.
card.good_to_know: The cathedral was built on the site of an old chapel or hermitage founded in 1108. The present church was begun in the second half of the 12th century, and work carried on until the 16th. King John I married Philippa of Lancaster here in 1387.

card.hook: From the pavement on Rua de Santa Catarina, Café Majestic looks like someone lifted a Parisian café and set it down in Porto. It's so full of decoration that you'll want to take more photos than you planned.
card.stand_here: Stand right at Café Majestic on Rua de Santa Catarina. The phone icon on the map is at the café itself, so there's no extra walk. Stay on the street by the entrance without blocking the door or the pavement, and angle your phone slightly along the façade to show its depth.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x if you can't step back far enough to fit the whole frontage. Switch to 1x for a more natural look, then try 2x or 5x (higher zooms depend on your phone) for the ornate details and signs.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines and line the edges of the building up with the vertical lines so it doesn't lean.

card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand on the street side of the pavement in front of the façade, while you stand by the entrance (not in the doorway), so they can step back and fit the whole frontage in.
card.rules_and_safety: The café is a private business, so check with them about photos inside and be polite to other guests. Skip the flash, and don't photograph other people's tables from the aisle, because staff may move you on.
card.challenge: Take one wide shot of the whole frontage with a little street life in it, then find the most ornate detail near the entrance and make it the star of a close-up.

It started as an exclusive place where the city's elite met. After decades of decline it was recognised as a building of national historical interest in 1983, and after a major restoration it reopened in July 1994 in its original Belle Époque style.

card.hook: Stand right under the Clérigos tower and you get a sore neck and about half a tower. Back off down the street and the whole thing pops up at the end of it like it was put there for you.

card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to fit the facade and tower together. Tap 2x if your phone has it for a tighter shot of the tower from the same spot.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines and line the tower up with a vertical line so it stands straight, and keep your phone level so it doesn't lean back.

card.hook: Porto has crammed a river, a giant iron bridge and a whole row of arcaded houses into one view, and the best way to enjoy it is to walk away from the crowd. Head for the quiet end of the waterfront and let the bridge do the showing off.
card.stand_here: Stand on Cais da Ribeira, at the eastern end of the riverside promenade, past the main tourist cluster. From there the square lies just to the north, so face along the Ribeira facades with the Dom Luís I Bridge behind them.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to fit the waterfront, the facades and the bridge into one frame. Switch to 1x for a more natural look at the house fronts, then try 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) to pick out the fountain or the Cubo da Ribeira.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and line the rows of facades up with them so the buildings stand straight, with the bridge in the upper part of the frame and the water or promenade in the lower part.
card.best_time: Go in the morning, when the Ribeira facades are lit directly and the riverside is quieter. The square is popular, so early is your best shot at a clear frame.
card.selfie_here: Head to Fonte do Cubo, the bronze cube fountain in the middle of Praça da Ribeira. Use the front camera at 0.5x and stand beside it with the narrow colourful houses stacked up behind you, ideally in the morning when it's less crowded.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand back from the cube fountain, roughly in the middle of the square, while you stand beside the fountain so it and the square's buildings both fit in the frame.
card.challenge: Get the bridge in the top of your frame and the water at the bottom, then wait for a gap in the crowd and see if you can get a person-free shot.
card.good_to_know: The buildings around the square were rebuilt with arcades after a fire in 1491. The square was reorganised between 1776 and 1782, and the medieval walls on the river side came down in 1821, which opened it up to the water. In the northern part there's a three-storey fountain from the 1780s with a statue of St John the Baptist.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on Cais da Ribeira, at the eastern end of the riverside promenade, past the main tourist cluster. From there the square lies just to the north, so face along the Ribeira facades with the Dom Luís I Bridge behind them.

card.hook: Two decks, one huge iron arch, and a Metro train gliding across the top like it owns the place. That's Dom Luís I Bridge, and the best view of it takes a steep climb and a rest at the top.
card.stand_here: Stand on the terrace in front of the Mosteiro da Serra do Pilar, on the Vila Nova de Gaia side. Face across the river towards the bridge, and the whole double-deck arch will be in front of you with Porto's hillside behind it.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x, which should fit most of the arch and the skyline. If the bridge gets cut off at the sides, drop to zoom 0.5x. Try zoom 2x to pick the bridge out against the hillside.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines and run the arch along the lower third of the frame so the city rises behind it.
card.best_time: Check on the day. Some guides say golden hour from the Gaia side, others say sunrise from the Ribeira side. If you want a night shot, make sure the bridge lights are on first, because one visitor found them switched off at midnight in summer.
card.selfie_here: Try the pedestrian walkway on the upper deck, beside the Metro tracks, with the Douro behind you. Use the front camera, switch to 0.5x if it's available, and let the river and a passing train sit over your shoulder. Jardim do Morro, at the Gaia end of the upper deck, should also work for a bridge-and-Porto selfie, but treat that one as a maybe.
card.ask_someone: Ask someone to stand by the riverside restaurants at Praça da Ribeira on the Porto side, facing the bridge, while you pose a few steps in front of them so the whole arch is behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: On the upper deck, stay on the pedestrian side and keep out of the Metro track lane. Hold on to children, because the Metro slows down on the bridge but trains still cross it.
card.challenge: Catch a Metro train crossing the upper deck with the whole arch still in the frame. Take a few shots as it passes, because one will be the winner.
card.good_to_know: When it was built, the bridge's 172-metre arch span was the longest of its type in the world. The upper deck opened in 1886 and the lower deck followed a year later. It was designed by Théophile Seyrig, who also designed the nearby Maria Pia Bridge, so the two look alike.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on the terrace in front of the Mosteiro da Serra do Pilar, on the Vila Nova de Gaia side. Face across the river towards the bridge, and the whole double-deck arch will be in front of you with Porto's hillside behind it.

card.hook: Plot twist: the famous iron bridge in most Porto photos isn't the one we're sending you to see. The slender Maria Pia arch is the quiet one upriver, and people mix it up with Dom Luís I all the time.
card.stand_here: Stand on the circular terrace in front of the Mosteiro da Serra do Pilar on the Vila Nova de Gaia side. Face east along the river: Dom Luís I is in the foreground, and the Maria Pia arch is further upriver.
card.zoom: Start at 1x to get both bridges and the Porto skyline in one postcard shot. Then try 5x if your phone has it to pull the little arch closer, and rest your phone on a wall or railing so it doesn't blur.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines, tap the arch, then drag the brightness slider a little darker so the sky keeps its colour and the iron stays dark.
card.best_time: Several guides suggest sunset, and since you're looking east, the evening light should fall on the bridge from behind you. Haze can flatten the view, so check the sky on the day.
card.selfie_here: Head to the Miradouro das Fontaínhas, which faces east over the river toward the Maria Pia Bridge, so you can turn around and have the bridge behind you. Use the front camera at 0.5x and keep the bridge over your shoulder. The river-facing lookout in the Jardins do Palácio de Cristal is another option, and one blogger calls it magical at sunset with a lovely view of the bridge.
card.ask_someone: Along the Gaia waterside promenade near the port wine cellars, find a spot where the bridge is in view, then hand your phone to a passer-by a few steps back and stand with the arch behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: You can't go onto the Maria Pia Bridge itself, so photos are taken from the riverbanks, from the Dom Luís I deck, or from a river cruise. If you shoot from the Dom Luís I deck, stay clear of the tram tracks.
card.challenge: Can you get both bridges in one shot and still make it obvious which one is Maria Pia? No pointing allowed.
card.good_to_know: Maria Pia was built in the 1870s and is attributed to Gustave Eiffel. King Luís I and Queen Maria Pia opened it in November 1878, and when it was finished it was the longest single-arch span in the world. The arch rises about 60 m above the river, and trains used it until 1991, when the São João Bridge took over. Dom Luís I came nine years later, about a kilometre downstream, and has two decks.

card.hook: Picture a big round church on a rocky hill, gazing across the river at Porto's old town like it's checking out the competition. At 36 m tall, it's hard to miss, and you get to stand right in front of it.
card.stand_here: Stand in Largo de Aviz, the open square in front of the round church, and face the Douro so the church is in front of you with the river, the Dom Luís I Bridge and Porto's riverfront behind it.
card.zoom: Step back a little, then start at zoom 0.5x to fit the whole church and plenty of sky. Standing too close at 0.5x exaggerates the tower. Switch to 1x for a more natural look, and if your phone has 2x or 5x, use it to pick out the bridge and riverfront.
card.make_it_pop: Tap the white stonework, then drag the slider down so the picture is a little darker and the sky keeps its colour.
card.best_time: Late afternoon gives softer light on the church. Sunsets here get very crowded, so arrive early if you want a clear spot.
card.selfie_here: Take your selfie on the big paved square in front of the church (Largo de Aviz), where the Douro and Porto make a good backdrop. Use the front camera, switch to 0.5x if your phone offers it, and keep the church over your shoulder. The long open sides of the square help keep other visitors out of your shot.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand in the small Jardim do Morro park below the monastery and frame the church above, while you pose with it rising behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: The approaches and steps can be steep, so take care on the climb. The square is a public viewpoint, but the church and the military area may have limited hours or tickets, so check the official site before you go.
card.challenge: Turn on gridlines and line the church up with a vertical line so the round walls stand straight, then see if you can squeeze the bridge into the same shot.
card.good_to_know: The church was inaugurated in 1672, and the monastery was later fortified and used in the wars of the 19th century. The cloister is also circular, with the same diameter as the church, which is unusual. It's part of Porto's UNESCO World Heritage listing, and the church still holds Sunday Mass.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand in Largo de Aviz, the open square in front of the round church, and face the Douro so the church is in front of you with the river, the Dom Luís I Bridge and Porto's riverfront behind it.

card.hook: There's a caped Don standing at the door of this port cellar, and he looks like he's checking tickets. He's also the best-known face on the Gaia side of the Douro, so he's your photo.
card.stand_here: Stand on the forecourt in Largo Miguel Bombarda, in front of the Sandeman cellar entrance and next to the Don statue. Face south-east towards the façade, with the Sandeman sign and the Don at the entrance.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to get the façade and the Don in together. If people or the building edges leave you no room, drop to 0.5x. For just the statue and the sign, try zoom 2x if your phone has it.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines, put the Don on one third line with the sign filling the upper part of the frame, and keep the building edges straight.
card.best_time: Go in the morning. The light is nicer and there are fewer people, and the tour groups tend to arrive around midday.
card.selfie_here: Take it at the Sandeman entrance on the Cais da Ribeira de Gaia promenade, at the lodge entrance with the Don behind you. Use the front camera, and if it has a 0.5x option, use it to fit the figure in over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand in front of the Sandeman Museum building (Largo Miguel Bombarda 3) so they can frame you with the whole cellar, but check that spot on the map first.
card.rules_and_safety: The forecourt is open to the public, but the cellar and its terraces may require a purchase. Check what's open before you plan a shot from inside.
card.challenge: Get the Don on a third line, the sign above him and the building edges dead straight, and see if you can do it before the midday crowd turns up.
card.good_to_know: This is the Sandeman cellar entrance on the Gaia side of the Douro, with Ribeira and the Dom Luís I Bridge across the water. Two addresses are in use for the cellar (Largo Miguel Bombarda 3 and 47), so check which one you're heading for. Want a different view afterwards? Cais de Gaia shows the lodge rooftops up close, and Jardim do Morro looks down on them from higher up.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on the forecourt in Largo Miguel Bombarda, in front of the Sandeman cellar entrance and next to the Don statue. Face south-east towards the façade, with the Sandeman sign and the Don at the entrance.

card.hook: From down on the water, the Ponte do Infante looks like someone drew one thin, pale pencil line across the gorge. It's a bit magic, and a bit "how is that staying up?"
card.stand_here: Stand on Passeio das Fontainhas, the riverside promenade on the Porto side directly below the bridge. Face south so the arch and deck rise above the river in front of you.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 0.5x to fit the whole arch and the river in one go. Then try 1x for a calmer, more natural view, and 2x to 5x (depending on your phone) to pick out the Dom Luís I bridge in the distance.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines, line the bridge deck up with a horizontal line so it sits level, and let the river fill the bottom third.
card.best_time: Sunset is the one guides recommend, when the bridge and river look their most atmospheric from this side. After the sun drops, switch on night mode and hold still for a couple of seconds.
card.selfie_here: Try Passeio das Fontainhas, where the bridge sits overhead as your backdrop. Use the front camera, switch to 0.5x if your phone offers it, and tilt up so the arch stays over your shoulder.
card.ask_someone: For a quieter option, go to the Avenida Gustavo Eiffel quayside east of the Dom Luís I Bridge and ask someone to shoot from the walkway, so the bridge's curve and the river below fit behind you.
card.rules_and_safety: Wear comfy shoes, because the walk can be uphill and uneven in places. Take care on any upper level of the bridges, where there's no barrier between trains and pedestrians, and keep an eye on kids near the bridge's car traffic.
card.challenge: Wait for a boat or a few people to wander into the water below, then catch them so everyone can see how huge this bridge is.
card.good_to_know: The bridge opened in 2003 and is 371 metres long, with a single arch spanning 280 metres. The deck sits 75 metres above the water, but the arch itself rises only about 25 metres. That makes it one of the flattest arches in the world for its length.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on Passeio das Fontainhas, the riverside promenade on the Porto side directly below the bridge. Face south so the arch and deck rise above the river in front of you.

card.hook: Here's a little Porto secret: the best way to photograph the grand avenue is to step away from the crowds and shoot it from the quieter square nearby. Statues up close, tall façades behind, and no one's elbow in your frame.
card.stand_here: Stand in Praça da Liberdade, with Avenida dos Aliados and its grand buildings about 150 m to the north of the stand-here point. Face north, towards the avenue.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x, which keeps the statues and the buildings together in one natural-looking shot. If the statues and the full height of the façades won't both fit, tap 0.5x. Use zoom 2x or higher (depends on your phone) to pick out details in the buildings.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines and line up the building edges with the vertical lines, so the tall façades stand straight instead of leaning.
card.best_time: Go in the daytime, when the light is good for photos.
card.selfie_here: Head up the avenue to the City Hall end and look for the large blue Porto sign, the classic photo prop, free to visit, with the grand façades as your backdrop. Use the front camera, try 0.5x, and hold your phone a little low so the sign and buildings fit over your shoulder. Check the map first, because the sign's exact spot isn't pinned down.
card.ask_someone: Ask a passer-by to stand at the end of the avenue near the Almeida Garrett statue and shoot back toward the City Hall, so the whole avenue shows with you in front of it.
card.rules_and_safety: Building works along the avenue may block some angles, and events can change things too, so check the situation on the day and be ready to move a few steps.
card.challenge: Put one statue in the corner of your frame, then see if you can keep every building edge perfectly on the gridlines. No leaning towers allowed!
card.good_to_know: Avenida dos Aliados is the grand avenue in the middle of Porto, with the City Hall rising behind its façades. It photographs well because of its strong, regular lines. Visitors have mentioned building works along the avenue, so some angles may change from day to day.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand in Praça da Liberdade, with Avenida dos Aliados and its grand buildings about 150 m to the north of the stand-here point. Face north, towards the avenue.
